newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies higher.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent a lb higher while pork belly futures were called 0.250 to 0.500 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Mostly steady cash hog calls and higher pork cutout values were seen as supporting factors in hog futures. Hog marketings have been running under expectations and the reduced slaughter is making for stronger cash pork values, especially in relation to high choice beef prices, analysts said.
However, some analysts again cited the large premium of futures to cash and reduced packer demand Monday due to the Veterans Day holiday, for resistance.
Pork cutout values were at highest levels since mid- October.

The lighter hog slaughter pace and rising pork prices were seen as supportive to pork belly futures. Cash belly prices rose to $64 per cwt on Friday, the highest level since October 14, and frozen belly storings have been running at a lighter-than-expected pace, analysts said.
The market also appears technically strong after the strong advance in futures last week, they added.
CME agricultural futures markets will close at 1200 CST in observance of the Veterans Day holiday.
